# The Rise of the Sea Principalities by Admiral Belchem Flotsome, CY 513

## 

## Keoland’s history of the Sea Principalities

In the annals of the kingdom of Keoland, the rise of the Sea Princes is a tale woven with the threads of ambition, cunning, and the relentless pursuit of power. During the zenith of Keoland's imperial aspirations, the buccaneers of the Azure Sea and Jeklea Bay found themselves in a fortuitous position. As Keoland's gaze was fixed northward, these audacious privateers, who would come to be known as the Sea Princes, seized the opportunity to grow in strength and wealth. Their leader, a noble-born captain of remarkable success, inspired the moniker that would become synonymous with their reign. From their island and mainland strongholds, they unleashed a reign of terror upon the coasts, stretching from Gradsul to Scant, and even beyond into the Sea of Gearnat and the Tilva Strait. Their unchecked exploits made them the scourge of the seas, feared by all who dared to cross their path.

 However, the tides of fortune are ever-changing, and as Keoland's imperial ambitions waned, the kingdom turned its attention back to the seas. The Keoish navy, bolstered by a squadron of Ulek warships, sought to curb the growing threat of the Sea Princes. The Battle of Jetsam Island marked a pivotal moment in this struggle, as the combined fleets clashed in a fierce contest of naval might. Though the Sea Princes emerged bloodied but unbowed, the encounter served as a wake-up call for their leaders. Realizing the need for a new strategy, the wiser captains retired to their mainland estates, entrusting their ships to capable lieutenants. No longer content with mere piracy, they embarked on expeditions to the Amedio coast, trading in rare woods, spices, ivory, and gold. Their mainland possessions soon eclipsed their island homes, and the Sea Princes transformed into a formidable sea power, with a small but efficient army and a reputation as relatively peaceful traders. Yet, beneath this veneer of respectability lay a dark secret—their continued reliance on slavery, a practice that drew the ire of the Yeomanry and threatened to fracture their unity.

Or so the historians of Keoland would have you believe . . . .

## The Kasakom War

All large empires see the history of the world through the lens of their own greatness. This is particularly true of Keoland, a nation ruled by the remnants of the great families of the Suel Empire, brought low centuries ago by the twin cataclysms and scattered throughout the Flanaess. Their account of the history of the Sea Princes contains some truths, but only enough to make their view of our nation plausible to other countries not as familiar with our ways or the accounting of our own struggles.

The true turning point in the Sea Princes' ascent came with their victory over the sahaugin kingdom of Kisakom, a formidable underwater realm that had long terrorized the shores of the Bay of Salinmoor. The sahaugin, known for their ferocity and cunning, had established a vast empire beneath the waves, with their capital near the Mirodian Deep of the Bay of Salinmoor. At first, their raids on the surface world were but a fraction of their activities, as they sought to expand their dominion over the Bay of Salinmoor below the waves, killing sea elves and other aquatic races indiscriminately. The deplorable activities of the sahaugin went unchecked for hundreds of years and by the early 400 CY, having eradicated their underwater rivals, they turned their attention to the surface. The began to terrorize the coastlines of the Bay of Salinmoor, raiding fishing villages, trade ports and fortifications alike. These activities were mostly ignored by the kings of Keoland, who had little interest in their most vulnerable province, Salinmoor.

Yet, the Sea Princes, with the aid of the Duke of Berghof, devised a plan to eradicate this threat. Armed with a mysterious yellow-white powder provided by the Duke, they launched a campaign of destruction against the sahaugin cities. The powder, lethal to the sahaugin upon contact with seawater, decimated their ranks, and between 427 and 430 CY, dozens of underwater cities were laid to waste. The island fortress of Pulchra Sententia, an ancient Suel fortification, served as the staging ground for these attacks, and for decades, the Sea Princes maintained vigilant patrols to guard against the sahaugin's return. The victory over Kisakom not only secured the Sea Princes' dominance over the seas but also marked the beginning of their golden age, as they rose to prominence and power in the years that followed.

## Abandonment of Pulchra Sententia

In the aftermath of the sahaugin's defeat and the rising tensions between Keoland and the Sea Principalities became exacerbated. In 453 CY, King Tavish III of Keoland led an army to Westkeep, where he was slain, bringing the hostilities between the two countries to a boiling point. Left with few military options, the kingdom of Keoland seized upon the opportunity to craft a narrative that would serve their own ends. They portrayed the Sea Princes as reckless marauders whose actions during the  Kasakom War had wrought ecological devastation upon the ocean and its floor. The mysterious powder, while effective against the sahaugin, had left a scar upon the marine environment, disrupting ecosystems and causing significant damage to aquatic animals living beneath the waves of the Bay of Salinmoor.

While there was a kernel of truth to this, Keoland's rulers spun tales of the Sea Princes' hubris, painting them as villains whose greed and ambition had led to the desecration of the seas. This propaganda served to rally support in the Ulek states against the Sea Princes, casting them as a common enemy to be vanquished instead of the protectors of the Bay of Salinmoor. The ecological destruction caused by the yellow-white powder lent credence to these claims, and the Sea Princes found themselves increasingly isolated on the world stage.

The Battle of Jetsam Island in 464 CY, where the Keoland and Ulek fleets engaged the Sea Princes' navy, was the ultimate outcome of Keoland’s efforts to propagandize the Kasakom War. While the battle was only a minor victory for Keoland, the admirals of the Sea Princes realized that they could not defeat the combined navies of Keoland and the Ulek states.

The Sea Princes, recognizing the shifting tides of fortune, briefly abandoned Pulchra Sententia and their patrols to satisfy the Ulek countries and create a truce between the countries. Though they reoccupied the island in 467 CY, the garrison was greatly reduced, and the vigilant patrols that had once guarded against the sahaugin's return were abandoned.

 The Sea Princes found themselves retreating from their aggressive tactics against the sahaugin. The political fallout of their campaign had left them vulnerable, and they turned their focus toward trade, seeking benefit from their new found safety. The island fortress of Pulchra Sententia, once a bastion of resistance against the sahaugin threat, became a relic of a bygone era.

![][image3]

## 

## Continuing conflicts

Although the Ulek states were satisfied with the abandonment of the tactics used at Pulchra Sententia, the Sea Princes and Keoland remained in constant rivalry and do so even today. The Sea Princes maintain their independence only through their growing naval power and the riches they generate through the extensive trade that pass through Monmurg.

While Keoland is a constant threat, more concerning is the resurgence of a sahaugin kingdom, like Kasakom. It is doubtful the Sea Principalities would be able to meet the threat of large sahaugin incursion without using the tactics of the Kasakom war. While the political difficulties with the Ulek states would be of concern, more concerning is the production of the yellow-white powder which is a mystery only the Duke of Berghof knows. Will he come to the aid of Monmurg and the outer islands in the future? Also, what will be his price?
